text:
ana: quick heads-up — seeing tail spikes when continuous-batching merges long-context reqs with short ones. timeline shows KV pager eviction + head-of-line blocking. attaching profiling summary in thread.
ben: can you share repro steps? is this on dedicated or hosted canary?
ana: canary dedicated pool (g5x2). repro is pretty small — send mixed-length traffic under continuous batching and watch kv_page_faults and batch_wait_time. config we used:\n\n```\nBATCH_MODE=continuous\nBATCH_MAX=32\nBATCH_MIN=1\nKV_SHARD=auto\n```\n\nand then send a few long prompts (~8k tokens) interleaved with short chat prompts. p95 jumps from ~80ms to >1s when a long context enters a batch.
chris: looked at perf trace. breakdown:
- batch_merge path waits on kv_pager_lock (~30-120ms)
- kv eviction routines trigger synchronous IO on the slow path for large KV sets
- memory shows fragmentation (many small free spans) -> allocator churn
metrics: kv_page_faults/sec spike, kv_eviction_count up 8x, batch_head_wait high, p99 occasionally OOM-retries.
chris: hypothesis: merging mixed sequence lengths causes the head request to stall while the merged batch's KV shard tries to reclaim and rehydrate pages. head-of-line is exacerbated by global eviction policy across shards.
taylor: interesting — might be two orthogonal issues: batching heuristic (merging by arrival only) and KV eviction granularity. if we split merges by max_context_size buckets we avoid evicting the cache used by the long request while short ones finish.
ben: did you try forcing batch-split by seq_len threshold? any diff?
ana: yes, quick test: split at 2048 tokens -> p95 improved ~2x in a small local run. but throughput dropped slightly. still need a better middle ground.
ben: can you paste the logs/snippet showing the pager stall?
ana: pasted minimal log excerpt below:\n\n```\n[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] batch_merge: merge_id=42 seqs=[128,128,8192] -> dispatch delayed 93ms waiting on kv_pager_lock shard=5\n[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] kv_pager: eviction triggered shard=5 evict_candidates=120 reclaimed=0 (fragmented)\n[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] kv_pager: fallback sync_read shard=5 pages=64 latency=85ms\n```\n
chris: that 'reclaimed=0 (fragmented)' line is telling. the eviction scanner couldn't build contiguous pages, so it fell back to slow path, hitting sync reads. we should record per-shard fragmentation histogram.
perf-bot: alert: hol_blocker_kv > 0.8 observed on canary pool (1800456805)
chris: possible quick mitigation ideas:
- change batching heuristic to avoid merging very long seqs with short ones (split by length buckets)
- implement per-shard LRU eviction with async prefetch to reduce sync reads
- add lightweight per-request KV reservation to avoid eviction while request still in-flight

ana: i'm going to run an A/B on canary with bucketed batching + kv_eviction async patch. capturing heap / jemalloc arenas + KV histograms. creating ticket #1234 for the experiment and will attach flamegraphs.
taylor: another angle — kernel selection / quantized path differences: quantized kernels use different cache stride and may change how much KV memory is touched per token, so fallback to float kernels might show different eviction patterns. worth checking before we finalise config change.
ben: thanks — if A/B looks good we can roll to dedicated pools, but keep hosted at default for now. please include a script to reproduce quick repro so SEs can validate customer cases.
ana: will do. ongoing — i'll post results + perf counters once the canary run finishes. :thumbsup:
